brief: Futures pricing implies a new Fed hiking cycle begins today, expected to deliver 95bps of tightening over the next 12 months. This would be the fourth hiking cycle this century and the 15th since the mid-1950s. Historically, hiking cycles have averaged 22 months (15 median) and 478bps (313bps median) of tightening. Their eventual magnitude is rarely apparent at liftoff, a 2011 New York Fed study found markets have consistently underpredicted cycle scale since the survey began in the early 1980s, though 2015 was a rare exception where markets priced a slightly higher terminal rate than was ultimately reached, and in 2022 markets again significantly underestimated the extent of tightening. The shallowest cycle on record is 1986-87, at 137bps across four moves. If current pricing and DB's economists are correct, this would become the shallowest hiking cycle in modern history, despite that history of underestimation at liftoff. Separately, recessions have historically followed the first hike by roughly 3 to 3.5 years on average, ranging from 11 months (1980 cycle to 1981 recession) to 86 months (1983 cycle to 1990 recession). The cycle that began in March 2022 is now 54 months old with no recession yet.
